title: DirectorMind General Seed Grammar v0.1
scope: Model-independent directing decisions. Project, format, duration, and genre constraints must be supplied by the target production.

sources.description: Selected directing and shot-design methods distilled from directing textbooks in geegl/directorskills. Method references guide decisions but do not prove authorial intent in any reference-film shot.
Good Omens S02E01 bookshop apology, three-person concealment plan, half-miracle ritual, and deadpan reaction sequence. Episode label and character initiative corrected during audit.
Good Omens S01E03 bandstand disagreement and separation. Speaker attribution and duration statistics corrected during audit.
Good Omens S02E01 record-shop and park-bench deadpan scenes. Only the cited shots support transfer; no whole-series claim is made.
Good Omens S01E04 pressure scene interrupted by a mundane outsider. Motion statistics and universal wording were rejected during audit.

rules.name: Locked script remains the story authority
rules.trigger: Every compilation from a LOCKED_SCRIPT or LOCKED_GOLDEN_CASE source.
rules.decision: Extract facts before directing. Preserve dialogue, visible text, reveals, causal order, relationship state, and ending hook; add only presentation decisions.
rules.coverage: Every source beat maps to at least one shot in source_coverage.
rules.blocking: Blocking may clarify source action but cannot create a new story event.
rules.pacing: Duration changes cannot delete a locked beat.
rules.sound: Do not add narration that explains hidden story facts.
boundaries: No script rewriting
No early reveal
No provider prompt syntax
rules.ai_risk: Compression can silently drop story beats.
rules.fallback: Reduce camera decoration or split a shot; never remove a locked beat.

rules.name: Geometry and axis before coverage
rules.trigger: Two or more interacting characters, especially dialogue or prop exchange.
rules.decision: Declare I/L/A geometry, the primary interaction axis, screen direction, and any justified axis change before selecting OTS, singles, or group coverage.
rules.coverage: Reuse the fewest camera positions that preserve space and reactions.
rules.blocking: Every move needs a story reason and updates the axis or relationship geometry visibly.
rules.pacing: Use establishing information only when the audience cannot infer the space from action and eyelines.
rules.sound: A sound or voice may establish an off-screen subject before a visual cut.
boundaries: I/L/A is a planning vocabulary, not a mandatory pose
Do not force OTS when clean singles express separation
rules.ai_risk: Multiple axes and unnecessary camera positions increase continuity failures.
rules.fallback: Return to one stable axis, one two-shot, and paired singles.

evidence.notes: Axis, I/L/A staging, and sightline boundaries.

rules.name: POV and reaction carry emotional meaning
rules.trigger: An event, line, or reveal changes relationship, knowledge, or emotional state.
rules.decision: Choose the scene POV and cut or hold on the listener whose reaction most changes audience understanding. Reaction can live inside a group shot; it is not automatically a new close-up.
rules.coverage: Reserve clean reaction coverage for the most consequential event points.
rules.blocking: Eyelines and listening behavior identify the active witness.
rules.pacing: Allow the event to land before the next explanatory line; length is scene-specific, not a fixed formula.
rules.sound: Use silence or low ambience when the audience needs to read the reaction.
boundaries: Do not interrupt peak physical action with compulsory reactions
Do not use reaction shots as emotional instruction without a story change
rules.ai_risk: Long close-ups are camera-simple but performance-sensitive.
rules.fallback: Shorten the held reaction or carry it in a stable two-shot while preserving the emotional beat.

evidence.notes: Jim's friendship line resolves through Crowley's rejection and Aziraphale's reaction.
Invitation, refusal, and listener reaction receive separate visual weight.

rules.name: Camera movement must mark a visible decision or spatial change
rules.trigger: A character enters, leaves, crosses a meaningful threshold, or makes a discrete decision that becomes action.
rules.decision: Keep camera and actors stable until movement has a narrative reason. Use one primary camera path synchronized with the motivated actor move.
rules.coverage: Static coverage is preferred for deadpan dialogue; movement is a scarce emphasis tool.
rules.blocking: Define actor start, trigger, path, and end before camera path.
rules.pacing: Motion begins and ends with the meaningful action.
rules.sound: Use movement foley or room-tone change to reinforce the state transition.
boundaries: Still-vs-motion applies to a decision, not any static scene
Do not move the camera only to add production value
rules.ai_risk: Actor and camera motion together can drift or expose geometry errors.
rules.fallback: Lock the camera and express the decision through one clear actor move or cut to the result.

evidence.notes: Motion is motivated choreography; still-vs-motion is limited to decision moments.

rules.name: Compose for the cut, not the isolated frame
rules.decision: Judge framing, look room, scale changes, screen direction, focus, and action endpoints by how adjacent shots connect.
rules.coverage: Every shot declares edit in/out and continuity in/out.
rules.blocking: End positions become the next shot's starting facts.
rules.pacing: Cut on a motivated look, action, line, sound, or state change.
rules.sound: Maintain ambience continuity unless a designed silence or sound bridge changes perspective.
boundaries: A beautiful frame that breaks continuity fails
Symmetry is allowed when repeated as a deliberate sequence language
rules.ai_risk: Independent generation encourages state reset between shots.
rules.fallback: Reduce state changes and reuse the last approved frame or declared close state as the next input anchor.

evidence.notes: Composition is evaluated through adjacent-shot relations.

rules.name: Treat supernatural absurdity with ordinary visual seriousness
rules.trigger: A powerful supernatural official applies sincere procedural logic to a tiny domestic or financial problem.
rules.decision: Keep performance and camera matter-of-fact; let incompatible logic and the human listener's reaction create comedy.
rules.coverage: Stable two-shot or OTS for exchange; clean single at the strongest logic mismatch; reaction hold after the absurd proposal.
rules.blocking: Use a mundane physical divider such as desk, counter, doorway, or table.
rules.pacing: Dialogue stays controlled; the reaction receives slightly more air than the punch line.
rules.sound: Natural room tone, object sounds, and no automatic comedy cue.
boundaries: Not for a magic spectacle whose value is visual transformation
Clean singles are a preference at mismatch peaks, not a ban on OTS
rules.ai_risk: Overplaying facial comedy turns deadpan into sketch acting.
rules.fallback: Use one restrained eyebrow/eye-line reaction and a short silent tail.

evidence.notes: Reference report supports matter-of-fact framing and delayed reaction; whole-series intent remains inferred.

rules.name: Parallel, low-contact staging for bureaucratic deadpan
rules.trigger: Two officials conduct a tedious handoff, report, or negotiation whose content is stranger than their manner.
rules.decision: Use parallel I-staging, restrained eye contact, mostly locked coverage, and one shared master to preserve institutional distance.
rules.coverage: Master plus limited singles or OTS; return to the master for silence or procedural closure.
rules.blocking: Characters sit or stand on the same directional line and avoid unnecessary facing or touching.
rules.pacing: Measured shots with small post-line tails; do not force rapid comedy cutting.
rules.sound: Plain ambience and dry voices; no espionage or fantasy scoring by default.
boundaries: Not for romantic connection or kinetic confrontation
Do not confuse total stillness with the still-vs-motion decision technique
rules.ai_risk: Long dialogue creates lip-sync and identity pressure despite simple geometry.
rules.fallback: Break long dialogue into stable singles and listener reactions while preserving the shared master at open and close.

evidence.notes: Park-bench mistaken rendezvous demonstrates parallel staging and deadpan reaction.

rules.name: Mundane interruption can deflate supernatural pressure
rules.trigger: A high-pressure supernatural confrontation has reached a sustained peak and a plausible outsider or ordinary malfunction can interrupt it.
rules.decision: Introduce the mundane interruption through sound or a clean insert, then hold the threatened and threatening characters sharing the same redirected attention.
rules.coverage: Interruption insert, synchronized group reaction, then a restrained aftermath shot.
rules.blocking: The interruption originates outside the confrontation axis and redirects eyelines together.
rules.pacing: Break the prior pattern; allow silence after the attention shift.
rules.sound: Drop score or tension texture and restore ordinary ambience.
boundaries: The interruption must arise from established space or situation
Do not use it to rescue a protagonist through arbitrary coincidence
Not for a payoff that requires sustained terror or action victory
rules.fallback: Use separate fixed reaction shots connected by the same off-screen sound and eyeline.

evidence.notes: A mundane outsider redirects all eyelines; prior report's motion percentages were rejected.

rules.name: Show comic surrender in an uninterrupted body-wide action
rules.trigger: A proud character consciously performs a safe, embarrassing act to concede or repair a relationship.
rules.decision: Give preparation room, show the act in an objective full-body frame, then cut to the other character's restrained satisfaction.
rules.coverage: Preparation close/medium, uninterrupted wide action, listener reaction.
rules.blocking: Performer occupies clear central space; observer stays outside the action lane.
rules.pacing: Hold before the act; do not fragment the act unless AI execution requires it.
rules.sound: Music may function as a bounded gag only if evidence and project tone support it; it starts and ends with the action.
boundaries: Not for coercive abuse, surrender under mortal threat, or humiliation without relational repair
One reference sequence does not create a universal rule
rules.ai_risk: Full-body irregular choreography is performance and continuity HIGH.
rules.fallback: Use an upper-body medium shot plus a separate observer reaction, preserving preparation and completion.

evidence.notes: Apology dance sequence; report's episode label corrected to S02E01.

rules.name: Triad alliance forms through two-plus-one reaction geometry
rules.trigger: Two characters negotiate responsibility for a third character who is physically present and cognitively out of step.
rules.decision: Establish three-person geometry, show the pair forming a temporary alliance in a two-shot, give the third character a clean interruption or reaction, then restore the three-shot for the shared decision.
rules.coverage: Three-shot establishment, pair two-shot, third-character single, pair reaction, three-shot close.
rules.blocking: The pair share one axis; the third character sits or stands off that axis until brought into the final arrangement.
rules.pacing: Pair dialogue may be tighter; the third character's interruption and pair reaction receive a pause.
rules.sound: Keep the third character's line clear and allow the pair's silent reaction to land.
boundaries: Not for three equal participants in a formal meeting
Do not mechanically copy the reference's parent-child metaphor
rules.ai_risk: Three identities, synchronized looks, and hand contact raise continuity risk.
rules.fallback: Split the three-shot into a pair two-shot and a clean third-character single; reserve physical contact for a static setup frame.

evidence.notes: Aziraphale proposes the half-miracle; Crowley agrees; the reference report reversed this initiative and was corrected.

rules.name: Overhead geometry separates a visible ritual from ordinary dialogue
rules.trigger: A real, visible supernatural ritual has a clear group arrangement and needs one spatially distinct emphasis shot.
rules.decision: Use a high or overhead locked wide only when the geometry and ritual state are legible; return to ordinary eye-level reactions afterward.
rules.coverage: Eye-level preparation, one overhead ritual shot, eye-level aftermath.
rules.blocking: Participants form a simple readable shape with stable contact and no extra motion.
rules.pacing: Hold long enough to read arrangement and effect; avoid repeating the angle without a new state.
rules.sound: Change sound texture only as much as the script's effect warrants.
boundaries: Top-Down is an angle, not camera movement
Not for dialogue-only magic
One ritual sequence provides LOW transfer confidence
rules.ai_risk: Three-person contact, exact geometry, and VFX are continuity HIGH.
rules.fallback: Use a locked frontal three-shot plus an insert of the shared prop or light change.

evidence.notes: The report labels several high-angle shots Top-Down; exact 90-degree geometry remains to be frame-verified.

rules.name: Relationship fracture uses clean singles, then spatial departure
rules.trigger: A previously allied pair makes an invitation, refuses it, and accepts separation without physical contact.
rules.decision: Use shared space or OTS while negotiation remains possible; isolate the vulnerable invitation, refusal, and wound in clean singles; return to spatial coverage for acceptance and departure, then hold on the person left behind.
rules.coverage: Shared/OTS negotiation, clean-single emotional wound, OTS or wide departure, retained-space aftermath.
rules.blocking: Distance grows through a motivated turn and exit; the remaining character does not chase or touch.
rules.pacing: Protect silence after the hurtful line and before departure; do not prescribe one universal number of seconds.
rules.sound: Delay score until the decision or exit if music is used; preserve ambience through the verbal wound.
boundaries: Clean singles do not replace every OTS after conflict
Audience inference of lying is not automatically dramatic irony
Foreground exit with held focus is advanced, not default
rules.ai_risk: Subtle micro-expression is performance HIGH; foreground crossing with focus transition is continuity HIGH.
rules.fallback: Use a static clean reaction, cut to a separate exit back, then return to the remaining character in a wider locked shot.

evidence.notes: The invitation, refusal, wound, and departure sequence was retained; speaker attributions in the source report were corrected during audit.
